sentence: Shuffle once a second for fourteen billion years, the age of the universe.
claim: The universe began around 13.8 billion years ago ('fourteen billion' is a rounding; the sum uses 13.8).
source_title: NASA Science, Universe overview (history of the universe)
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. The page states 'Around 13.8 billion years ago, the universe expanded faster than the speed of light for a fraction of a second' (cosmic inflation, i.e. the start); it is a cosmologists' estimate.
builder_read: "Around 13.8 billion years ago, the universe expanded faster than the speed of light for a fraction of a second, a period called cosmic inflation."

sentence: Even then, you cover less than one part in a trillion trillion trillion of the orders.
claim: 8.2e9 people x 13.8e9 years x 3.156e7 s = 3.6e27 shuffles; 3.6e27 / 8.07e67 = 4.4e-41, which is less than 1 part in 10^36 (a trillion trillion trillion).
source_title: Derivation (calc.py): 52! = 8.07e67 and the counts in the claim; no outside page
note: DERIVATION from 52! (= 8.07e67); not taken from the Factorial page. The inputs (8.2e9 people, 13.8e9 years) are claims c4 (people) and c5 (years). OPEN until a person re-does the sum.

sentence: Your shuffle is almost certainly the first of its kind.
claim: If a shuffle is fair and uniform, the chance that it matches any specific earlier one is 1 in 52!; against all 3.6e27 shuffles in the thought experiment it is 4.4e-41. (The chance that any two of those ever match is about 8e-14, by the birthday bound N^2 / (2 x 52!).)
